chains.title: C228T creates a de novo GGAA ETS site bound by GABPA (with GABPB1), reactivating TERT
chains.element: TERT core promoter cCRE EH38E3622530 (PLS), chr5:1294945-1295294
chains.cell_type: Glioblastoma tumour cells (also melanoma, bladder urothelium)

links.claim: ENCODE GABPA ChIP-seq peaks in two biosamples (HepG2, SK-N-SH) directly contain chr5:1295113, so GABPA occupies this base; within the ETS/GGAA specificity group GABPA is chosen on this direct occupancy evidence plus its expression in glioblastoma (15.52 TPM, rank 303/1626 TFs), not on memory alone. The alt (A) allele is predicted to bind more strongly because it converts the sequence to a GGAA ETS core, but no QBiC-SELEX row or allele-specific binding assay was provided, so the direction of the allelic effect is inferred, not shown, and coverage is not_checked. Note the peaks are from non-glioblastoma, likely wild-type-promoter lines, so they show GABPA can reach this promoter region but not allele specificity.

The variant lies inside an active promoter-like cCRE (EH38E3622530, PLS; DNase z 4.8, H3K4me3 z 4.5, H3K27ac z 4.2) annotated as the TERT promoter; these z-scores are maxima over ENCODE biosamples, not glioblastoma-specific.

TERT's TSS is 0.0 kb from the variant and the cCRE is annotated to TERT; all other protein-coding genes are >=50 kb away. This is proximity plus promoter annotation only, with no eQTL or perturbation link for this somatic base.

The relevant cells are IDH wild-type glioblastoma and melanoma tumour cells, where TERT promoter mutations are among the most frequent alterations (50-82% of melanoma), and where GABPA is expressed at 15.52 TPM (58.4th percentile across DepMap lines). No evidence here is specific to bladder.

Reactivated TERT restores telomerase activity and prevents replicative senescence, permitting unlimited proliferation; conversely, lowering TERT triggers senescence in melanoma cells. The senescence evidence is from a USP10/FOXM1 study, not from this variant.

chains.title: The created GGAA site is bound mainly by ETS1 rather than GABPA, activating TERT
chains.cell_type: Glioblastoma and melanoma cells with high ETS1

links.claim: The alt allele creates a GGAA core read by the shared ETS specificity group; within that group ETS1 is selected on measured expression (61.01 TPM, rank 43/1626 TFs in glioblastoma, 73.9th percentile), which is far higher than GABPA, and because ETS1 binds single GGAA sites without GABP's tetramer requirement. No ETS1 ChIP peak at this base and no QBiC-SELEX row were provided, so coverage is not_checked and binding is inferred.
The created site lies in the active TERT promoter cCRE with strong DNase/H3K4me3/H3K27ac maxima.
TERT is at 0 kb and is the cCRE's annotated gene; proximity only.
ETS1 is abundantly expressed in glioblastoma lines, and TERT promoter mutations are frequent in melanoma and IDH-wt GBM, so an ETS1-driven effect is plausible in these lineages.
Increased TERT transcription sustains telomerase and blocks senescence.

chains.title: The ref G allele binds a repressive factor whose loss de-represses TERT
chains.cell_type: Glioblastoma, melanoma and bladder tumour cells

links.claim: Under this alternative the G>A change destroys a ref-preferring site for a repressive promoter factor such as ZNF143, so activation would be loss of repression rather than gain of an ETS site. No binding evidence of any kind supports this: the only ChIP data at this base are GABPA peaks, which argue for the activator-gain reading. Coverage is not_checked and the TF choice is a placeholder.
The variant lies in the TERT promoter cCRE; the CTCF z of 2.0 is a weak maximum over biosamples and does not itself indicate repressor occupancy.
TERT's TSS coincides with the element; proximity only.
TERT is repressed in normal somatic cells and reactivated in these tumour types; the cited evidence gives mutation frequency, not loss of a repressor.
De-repression of TERT restores telomerase and blocks senescence.

grades_v0.reason: E01 is only a VEP consequence and says nothing about GGAA creation or GABPA binding. No QBiC-SELEX, ChIP or allele-specific data are cited. The GABPA choice rests on memory, and coverage is 'not_checked' with no lookup.

E03 shows the variant inside PLS cCRE EH38E3622530 with high DNase, H3K4me3 and H3K27ac z-scores, and E01 shows a promoter regulatory feature. These are maxima over biosamples, not glioblastoma-specific, so this is epigenomic context only. It is adequate for the element claim.

E02 shows TERT at 0 kb from the TSS and E03 lists TERT as a nearby gene. This is proximity only, with no eQTL or perturbation linking this variant to TERT expression. The proximity is strong for a promoter.

E04a (melanoma, 50-82%) and E04f (IDH-wt GBM) show TERT promoter mutations are frequent, but they do not show C228T specifically, and nothing is cited for bladder. No cell-type-specific expression or TF expression is given.

E04a links promoter mutation to telomerase activation. E04e shows USP10/FOXM1 loss lowers TERT and triggers senescence, but this is not about the variant or GABPA. The chain is consistent but indirect.

E01 is only a VEP consequence and says nothing about ETS1 binding. ETS1 is chosen from the ETS group on expression claims from memory, with no expression lookup or binding data, and coverage is unchecked.
E03 shows the variant in an active PLS cCRE with strong chromatin marks.
E02 and E03 show TERT is the nearest and annotated gene. This is proximity only, with no QTL or perturbation evidence.
E04a gives only the frequency of TERT promoter mutation in melanoma. It does not show ETS1 expression or ETS1 dependence, which the claim rests on.
E04a and E04e are generic TERT/telomerase evidence and are not specific to ETS1.
E01 does not bear on ELK4 binding. The ELK4 choice and its MAPK responsiveness come from memory, and no lookup was done.
E01 and E03 place the variant in the TERT promoter-like cCRE.
E02 shows TERT 0 kb from the TSS. This is proximity only.
E04f shows only that TERT promoter mutations are frequent in GBM. It shows nothing about MAPK activity or ELK4 in these cells.
E04a and E04e are generic TERT evidence. Nothing links signal-dependent induction to the phenotype.

The text itself says no ZNF143 data exist. E01 does not support a ref-allele repressor, and the direction (ref binds more) conflicts with the best-known gain-of-ETS mechanism. ZNF143 is an arbitrary pick and coverage is unchecked.
E03 supports the promoter cCRE, but CTCF z 2.0 is a low-level maximum over biosamples and does not indicate repressor occupancy. The claim over-reads it.
E02 and E03 show TERT proximity, with no functional link to this variant.
E04a shows frequency of mutation, not that repression is lost. It does not support loss of a repressor.
E04a and E04e show telomerase and senescence generally. They do not discriminate de-repression from activator gain.

PMID 42807929 (2026): USP10 stabilizes FOXM1 through KAT5-mediated acetylation to suppress cell senescence and promote melanoma malignant progression.
PMID 42859331 (2026): CDKN2A deletion associated with poor prognosis in patients with TERT promoter wild-type, IDH wild-type glioblastoma.

A major molecular feature of melanoma is abnormal telomerase activation; this is most often caused by telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT) promoter mutations, which occur in 50-82% of cases and are the most common noncoding alteration in this cancer.
CDKN2A and CDK4 mutations act through UV-dependent and cell cycle disruption pathways, while BAP1, POT1, and TERT mutations are considered UV-independent.
The single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) rs2853669, also located in the TERT promoter, may influence telomerase activity, though its clinical relevance in GBM remains unclear.

Patients carrying the SNP and TPM on the same allele (C/C and T/C cis) had shorter overall survival than those carrying them on different alleles (T/T or T/C trans; 19 vs 25 months, p = 0.048), and TERT expression was also lower in this group (p = 0.038).
Additionally, loss of either USP10 or FOXM1 suppresses the expression of the downstream target Telomerase reverse transcriptase (TERT), triggering cellular senescence.

TERT promoter (TERTp) mutations are among the most frequent molecular alterations in isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) wild-type glioblastoma (GBM), yet the molecular profiles and prognostic implications associated with TERTp status remain incompletely characterized.
